text:
Arjun: Proposal — introduce an 'entropy-watch' canary gate for upcoming quantized-v4p2 onboard. Combine distributional shift (KL on logits), sample-level concordance, and a small hallucination probe. Auto-fallback if the composite score crosses the threshold. Short version: more signal diversity than a pure MRR gate. Thoughts?
Maya: hmm interesting. can you sketch the exact signals & thresholds? :eyes:
Arjun: sure. rough idea: 1) KL_div = symmetric KL between baseline logits and candidate logits (masked to top-200 tokens) 2) Concordance = fraction of samples where candidate top-1 matches baseline top-1 on structured tasks (QA, extract) 3) Halluc_probe = small set (500 samples) of targeted hallucination prompts measured by human-labeled or high-precision detectors. 4) MRR_delta still included.
Arjun: initial trigger logic (proposal): 
```
score = 0.4 * normalized_MRR_drop + 0.35 * normalized_KL + 0.25 * normalized_halluc_rate
if score >= 0.65 => immediate autofallback
if score in [0.45,0.65) for 3 consecutive 1-minute windows => alert + pause traffic
```
Maya: can you define normalization? e.g., how does a 1.0% MRR drop compare to KL 0.08?
Tom: practical suggestion: normalize each metric to a 0-1 clip using historical 99th percentiles per cohort. so normalized = min(max((value - baseline)/p99, 0), 1). keeps mixing stable across slices.
Sasha: worried about false positives on low-volume slices (longdocs). we should add a min-requests cutoff and volume-adjusted variance dampening. otherwise KL noisy.
Arjun: agreed — require min 1k requests over the window or fall back to longer windows (5m). also apply a dampening factor alpha = 1/sqrt(n_requests) when n_requests < 2k.
CI-bot: canary-run: baseline=v4p1@2026-02-10, candidate=v4p2-quant@2026-03-01, sample_size=5k, MRR_delta=-1.12%, KL_median=0.094, halluc_probe_rate=0.68%, concordance=92.3% (QA/extract).
Joel: given those numbers, what's score per your formula?
Arjun: quick calc (rough): normalized_MRR_drop ~= 0.7 (p99 ~1.6%), normalized_KL ~= 0.47 (p99 ~0.2), normalized_halluc ~= 0.34 (p99 ~2.0) => score ~= 0.4*0.7 + 0.35*0.47 + 0.25*0.34 = 0.28 + 0.165 + 0.085 = 0.53 => in the 'pause & investigate' band.
Sasha: so it wouldn't autofallback immediately, but we'd get an alert. good. Still want an early-warning channel for longdocs where concordance drops >3% even if MRR steady.
Tom: propose a secondary hard gate: if concordance_drop >= 3.5% AND halluc_probe_rate >= 0.5% => immediate autofallback (because those indicate semantic regressions).
Maya: what about tying to user-impact buckets? e.g., make threshold stricter for high-value cohorts (payments, legal) and laxer for casual chat. We should surface per-cohort weights in the score calculation.
Arjun: yes — plan: compute cohort_weight (0.5..2.0) and multiply final score by cohort_weight before comparing to thresholds. default weight=1.0. 
Arjun: runbook notes: - require at least 2 consecutive windows exceed threshold before full traffic cutover - auto-create a rollback ticket with sample diffs + representative prompts - store per-candidate artifacts (top-k logits, samples) for replay & WL debugging
deploy-bot: offline-sim completed: 5 simulated canary runs (5k samples each) -> 2/5 runs would have triggered immediate autofallback under Tom's secondary gate; 3/5 would have entered the investigate band. details: https://redwood.internal/sims/4232100000 (private) :paperclip:
Joel: ok next steps? I can help run a 50k stress sim to sanity-check p99 normalization and p99 values per cohort.
Maya: please also add a low-latency alert path for SRE (pager) only if autofallback occurs; otherwise push to #eng-ml with @oncall SRE mention.
Arjun: perfect. I'll draft an RFC with the equations, threshold defaults, cohort weighting plan, and a small smoke run scheduled tomorrow PST. cc @SRE on alerting config. 
Sasha: :thumbsup: schedule the smoke at low-traffic hours.
Arjun: thanks all — will post the RFC link when ready.
